ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended; Criminal Code, R.S.C., 1985, c. C-46, ss. 355 and 462.31 (money-laundering offences); Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Suspicious Transaction Reporting Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57, Part 9.1 (Transparency Register), as amended by the Business Corporations Amendment Act (No. 2), 2019, S.B.C. 2019, c. 8; Business Corporations Regulation, B.C. Reg. 65/2004.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled identity document (passport) for each director, officer, and 25%+ UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notary public plus designated apostille authority in the document's jurisdiction of origin (e.g., Global Affairs Canada or applicable provincial authentication office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization depending on whether the issuing jurisdiction is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified corporate register extract or certificate of good standing for any corporate shareholder or non-natural-person UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry in the jurisdiction in which the corporate UBO or shareholder is incorporated
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization depending on the issuing jurisdiction's treaty status

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certificate of incumbency or register of directors/officers for any corporate shareholder or external professional body governed by a foreign legal entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or statutory officer of the foreign corporate shareholder, notarized and apostilled by the competent authority of the foreign jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization depending on the issuing jurisdiction's treaty status

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Irrevocable power of attorney and BC registered agent consent for service of process
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notarized grantor instruction from the incorporator/shareholders, countersigned by the licensed BC registered agent accepting service
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for the notarized grantor signature if executed outside Canada

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and Sanctions lists, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada's consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA), the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, and all available provincial/federal domestic PEP databases. Screening must include a five-year lookback for adverse media, current PEP status, and negative verification of any PEP or sanctions match prior to incorporation. Enhanced due diligence is triggered by any risk indicator, nominee ownership, unexplained wealth, or sanctions/PEP flag.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online (Corporate Registry, Government of British Columbia, accessible through OneStop Business Registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in Roman script or submitted with an English/French transliteration for registry indexing. The statutory legal element for an unlimited liability company must appear in the name as 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'ULC' or another prescribed abbreviation authorized under the Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57. The name must be distinguishable from all existing corporate and registered names in the BC Corporate Registry and must not be misleading or contrary to public policy.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may submit an administrative reconsideration request through BC Corporate Online or by written submission to the BC Registrar of Companies within 30 days of the rejection notice, attaching evidence of distinctiveness, consents from regulatory bodies, trademark registrations, or revised name alternatives. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, judicial review may be pursued before the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241. A valid name reservation may be renewed once for an additional 56-day period by filing a renewal request before expiry and paying the applicable renewal fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office address is mandatory and must be a physical address in British Columbia at which legal process can be served. A licensed BC corporate services agent's street address may be used; however, a pure virtual mail-forwarding address without a physical corporate records office does not satisfy the BC Business Corporations Act. For the low-risk executive-search/headhunting industry, so long as a BC agent maintains a physical office and the company's corporate records are accessible, the use of a virtual or agent-provided registered office is generally acceptable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for this industry: estimated 3–5% annualized probability of an unannounced physical inspection based on FINTRAC and BC Corporate Registry risk-based supervision of low-risk administrative and consulting entities. The likelihood increases materially to approximately 15% or higher if the UBO is a PEP, a sanctions match is identified, or the registered agent is known to provide only virtual service without substantive physical records.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: BC corporate name search and reservation (Corporate Online, one name request)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee under the Business Corporations Regulation, B.C. Reg. 65/2004

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: BC Unlimited Liability Company (ULC) incorporation filing under the Business Corporations Act, inclusive of certificate of incorporation and notice of articles
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory government fee schedule; expedited filing fee, if used, is additional

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and records office address in British Columbia (annual subscription through a licensed BC registered agent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed BC registered agent / corporate services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for registered-office and corporate-records services in British Columbia

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Stage 1 legal due-diligence package: UBO identification and ownership-tree analysis, PEP/sanctions screening, ULC constitutional document drafting, pre-incorporation resolutions, and transparency register scaffold
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Engaged law firm (ULC and AML/CFT specialist)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing fixed-fee or partner-hour market benchmark for Canadian pre-incorporation and AML/CFT compliance work

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, translation, and apostille or consular legalization of foreign identity and corporate documents for non-resident directors, incorporators, and UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, certified translator, and designated competent authority in each source jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notary tariff plus apostille fee schedule of the issuing jurisdiction, with 90-day document validity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation of the internal BC transparency register and related corporate-record filings (no separate Part 9.1 public filing fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Legal counsel or licensed registered agent (no direct BC registry fee for Part 9.1 transparency register)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Service fee based on standard corporate-regulatory compliance work

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 19, s. 10 and related incorporation, registered office, directors and records provisions; Companies Regulation, B.C. Reg. 221/2020.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, Corporate and Land Register Branch, Ministry of Finance, Government of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles filed with the Incorporation Application through BC Corporate Online; Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the BC Business Corporations Act, and no escrow account or capital deposit is mandated for an Unlimited Liability Corporation. Shares may be issued for any lawful consideration without par value, provided the Articles designate the company as an unlimited liability company and shareholders remain liable as prescribed by the Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS the Certificate of Incorporation was issued for [Company Name], an unlimited liability company organized under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia); RESOLVED, that 100 common shares are issued to the founding subscriber for lawful consideration, in accordance with the subscription ledger; RESOLVED, that the registered office and records office are established at [Street Address], [City], British Columbia; RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Name] is appointed Corporate Secretary, and [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until the next annual general meeting; RESOLVED, that the authorized banking signatories and professional external advisors be engaged to open bank accounts and administer statutory filings as required. This resolution is effective as of the date of incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search, Reservation and Legal Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry / BC Corporate Online, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, British Columbia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed corporate name candidates through the BC Registry Name Request system. Ensure each name is distinct, compliant with BCBCA naming rules, and does not contravene protected or misleading word restrictions. Obtain the name reservation approval and retain the reservation reference for the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Consent or authorization for any distinctive name component
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is refused, submit an administrative reconsideration request to the Corporate Registry, file a modified name, or instruct the registry to convert the reservation to an alternative approved name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Online Registrations, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, British Columbia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and file the Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles electronically. The Articles must confirm the unlimited liability company structure, share capital with no par value, initial directors, and registered office address. Pay the prescribed fee and await the Registrar's Certificate of Incorporation, which creates the corporation upon issuance.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director for each initial director
Beneficial ownership transparency confirmation and registrable person declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or queried, correct the flagged deficiencies and re-file the amended Notice of Articles within the response period; alternatively, submit a formal administrative explanation to the Corporate Registry seeking registrar approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office, Records Office and Statutory Minute Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry filing and maintenance regime; corporate legal agent or law firm acting as registered records office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the registered office is a physical street address in British Columbia and the records office is located at the same or another physical address in the province. Complete the statutory minute book containing the incorporation documents, advance consents, share subscription register, directors register, officers register, and initial corporate governance resolutions. File any change of registered office promptly with the Corporate Registry.
required_dossiers: Confirmation of physical registered office address
Shareholders register and share subscription ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Corporate Registry issues an administrative query regarding the registered office or records, submit a corrected Notice of Change and a supporting declaration from the office holder within the stated cure period to prevent administrative dissolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax, Payroll and Municipal Business Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online; BC Ministry of Finance; municipal business licensing office; WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the incorporated ULC with the Canada Revenue Agency for a federal Business Number, including corporate income tax, GST/HST, and payroll program accounts if applicable. Register with the BC Ministry of Finance for any applicable provincial tax accounts, obtain the required municipal business licence for the headhunting office, and, if employees are engaged, register with WorkSafeBC for occupational injury compensation coverage.
required_dossiers: Board resolution authorizing tax registrations and banking authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA registration is delayed due to identity or document mismatch, use the CRA Online Document Verification Service or visit a Tax Services Office with certified corporate documents; if municipal licensing is delayed, apply for an interim permit or written zoning confirmation pending full approval.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Employment Standards Branch, Ministry of Labour, Government of British Columbia
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Recruitment Agency Licence — Private Employment and Recruitment Agency Licensing Regime under the Employment Standards Act (British Columbia)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy, Environmental Protection Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — administrative office-based headhunting operation; no full EIA or registration certificate required for ordinary office occupancy.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or point-source emission thresholds apply to executive-search office activity. The operation must comply with municipal sewage and stormwater bylaws, the BC Recycling Regulation, and standard municipal solid waste and e-waste handling requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal fire safety inspection and occupancy permit issued under the BC Fire Code; structural load certification where heavy office equipment or secure records vaults are installed; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance; emergency evacuation plan, fire extinguisher compliance, and first aid equipment per workplace size.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal income tax and GST/HST, via Business Registration Online (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/business-number.html); British Columbia Ministry of Finance for BC Provincial Sales Tax and Employer Health Tax, via eTaxBC and the BC OneStop Business Registry (https://onestop.ca/).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); FX administration is shared with the Department of Finance Canada, the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for transaction monitoring and EFT reporting, and the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for cross-border currency declaration. Prudential bank supervision rests with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI). Canada maintains no dedicated exchange-control office.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for both current and capital account items. The Canadian dollar floats freely and no exchange-control approval or conversion license is required for inbound equity, shareholder loans, retainer receipts, dividend remittances, or liquidation distributions. Profit remittance from the ULC to non-resident shareholders is subject only to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (statutory 25%, treaty-reduced under Canada-US Treaty Article X to 5% for a 10% or greater corporate shareholder and 15% otherwise), administered via CRA Forms NR301/NR302 at the paying bank; no FX hurdle applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender window, minimum conversion ratio, or mandatory repatriation for export or cross-border service proceeds (executive search retainers). Foreign currency may be held indefinitely in domiciliary accounts. Administrative reporting applies: single cross-border electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more are reportable to FINTRAC, and physical currency conveyance of CAD 10,000 or more must be declared to CBSA.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rated MEDIUM for low-value operational receipts (the mandated Wise B2B rail) and LOW for capital escrow, reserve concentration, or core clearing. Legal constraints: (1) any offshore EMI accepting CAD/USD for a Canadian entity must hold a FINTRAC money-services business registration; (2) retail payment service providers must comply with the Bank of Canada Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) registration regime; (3) EMI balances carry no CDIC deposit insurance and offer no credit relationship; (4) an EMI may not be used to segment wire activity or circumvent FINTRAC EFT reporting above CAD 10,000. Recommended architecture: Wise B2B for retainer intakes with daily sweeping into an RBC operational account; escrow and liquidity reserves remain exclusively with a Schedule I bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid mandate. A BC-incorporated ULC with at least one Canadian-resident director may complete remote onboarding with a video verification and a notarized corporate records kit at RBC, TD, or BMO. Fully non-resident shareholder/director structures (the typical US-parent ULC profile) require physical presentation of government-issued ID by at least one director or authorized signatory at a Canadian branch (or at an acceptable Canadian consular office), plus certified true copies for all other UBOs. Completely remote opening without any Canadian nexus is rated LOW feasibility; onboarding success is materially improved through an existing Canadian banking relationship or a funded professional intermediary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder with opaque corporate chain and unlimited-liability equity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: BC Corporate Online certified records (Notice of Articles, Register of Directors, Register of Shareholders), UBO breakdown to natural persons, tax-residence certificates for each UBO, Canadian counsel legal opinion on ULC validity, current board resolution naming signatories, and parental financial statements where the shareholder is a corporation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP exposure — executive search mandates place politically exposed persons as clients, candidates, or shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed PEP declarations for all UBOs and senior candidates, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds files for retainer payments, engagement letters with the search mandate, independent background-screening reports, and an ongoing PEP monitoring covenant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty exposure to sanctioned jurisdictions or OFAC/Sanctions Act-listed individuals
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Zero-risk policy certificate, consolidated OSFI/UN/OFAC sanctions screening output, client-territory exclusion schedule, and model client contract clause permitting immediate termination on sanctions grounds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of fintech EMI (Wise B2B) for retainer collections pending sweep to the ULC account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EMI FINTRAC MSB registration certificate, transaction-flow diagram with audit trail, signed daily-sweep instruction, and attestation that the EMI will not be used to disaggregate or reconstruct transactions above the CAD 10,000 reporting threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-flow anomaly for ISIC 7830 — sizeable offshore research-subcontractor vendor payments with thin documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed client retainer agreements, fixed-fee schedules and placement invoices, OECD/Canada section 247 transfer-pricing documentation, invoices from each research subcontractor, and CRA business number verification for the ULC.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign-parent equity injection into the BC ULC clears via SWIFT MT103 (or Fedwire with Canadian correspondent) into the ULC CAD/USD account at a Schedule I bank. Canada has no national FX purpose-code registry; banks accept SWIFT transaction-type codes and free-format narrative, with the recommended purpose reading 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION - ULC SUBSCRIBED SHARE CAPITAL' and a reference to the BC Business Corporations Act Notice of Articles if issuance alters share capital. Receiving-bank verification pack: certified Notice of Articles, board resolution authorizing issuance and signatories, updated shareholder register, UBO declaration, and US tax-pack references (Form 5471/8858) where US counsel directs. Single EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more are FINTRAC-reportable; no central-bank permit or conversion approval is required, and CAD/USD conversion executes at market rate with LVTS same-day settlement for domestic legs.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for a headhunting operating model: (1) domestic payables, payroll, and refunds settle via Payments Canada LVTS wire (CAD 100,000+) or standard EFT; (2) cross-border fee splits, subcontractor research fees, and retainer refunds clear via SWIFT MT103 with UETR reference; (3) a standby letter of credit (SBLC) is offered where a client requires performance security on retainer prepayment; a documentary commercial LC is rated not applicable for service-based executive search revenue. All outbound EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more carry FINTRAC reporting obligations; USD-to-CAD conversion occurs through the bank dealing desk with auto-sweep of the USD collection account into the CAD operating account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD FX forwards (vanilla outright; typical tenor 1-24 months) - fully permitted for retainer-pipeline FX exposure
FX swaps and swap rollovers - permitted for short-dated liquidity alignment at a Schedule I bank dealing desk
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD fixed-floating) - permitted for hedging longer-dated ULC intercompany loan balances
Currency options and zero-cost collars (CAD/USD) - permitted for contingent placement-fee receivables

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) - permissible only for restricted non-convertible currency pairs (e.g., CNY, KRW, RUB, BRL) via a Schedule I dealer; not applicable to CAD/USD where a deliverable forward market exists

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 calendar months after each anniversary of the company's recognition date, every year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing blocks issuance of Certificate of Compliance. Failure to file for two consecutive years permits the Registrar to strike-off or dissolve the ULC; reinstatement requires formal corporate restoration and penalty fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including British Columbia provincial corporate tax levy)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency; BC Ministry of Finance administered through the CRA coordinated tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after each taxation year-end. For a December 31 year-end, filing is due June 30 of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty equal to 5% of unpaid tax, plus 1% per full month up to 12 months. Interest accrues on unpaid balances; continued failure can lead to arbitrary reassessment and criminal prosecution for willful non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholder Resolution / ULO Confirmation (internal corporate record confirming members and any shares transferred)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed with a government body; retained in the statutory minute book and made available for regulator inspection under BC Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approved at each annual general meeting or by written resolution within 15 months of the previous annual meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government penalty; failure to maintain accurate member and transparency registers is an offense under the BC BCA and may prevent completion of capital transactions, including share transfer closings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the BC Business Corporations Act, a private ULC may dispense with an auditor by unanimous shareholder resolution. Mandatory audit applies if the ULC is an offering (public) corporation, if shareholders holding at least 1% of votes require an audit, or if the Registrar of Companies directs an audit. No specific revenue threshold is prescribed for a BC private unlimited liability corporation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public (offering) ULCs must prepare financial statements under IFRS. Private BC ULCs may use Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE). Tax records must support the T2 filing and comply with Income Tax Record Requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: BC BCA requires a transparency register of significant individuals (UBOs) showing at least 25% direct or indirect control. The register must be updated within 14 days of the company becoming aware of a share transfer or control change. At each annual meeting the directors must confirm the register is accurate and note any transfers. In a ULC this confirmation is especially relevant because members are jointly and severally liable for corporate liabilities; the register ties the shareholder per shareholding period and fiduciary exposure.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book containing resolutions of shareholders and directors
Financial records supporting T2 and audited/reviewed financial statements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 250–750 annual registered office and corporate agent maintenance fees for a British Columbia ULC
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 5,000–15,000 for a full statutory audit when required; 1,500–3,500 for a review engagement when audit waiver applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% aggregate statutory rate (federal Part I 15% + British Columbia provincial general corporate income tax 12%; the BC small business rate of 2% is unavailable because the ULC is not a Canadian-controlled private corporation)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canada provides no statutory tax holidays or IP box regimes. The ULC executive-search agency is taxed at the 27% aggregate rate on worldwide income. Principal reliefs: ordinary deductibility of recruiter salaries, independent contractor fees, business development costs, software/telecom expenses and leasehold rentals; capital cost allowance on IT equipment and furniture; interest deduction on arm's length debt; foreign tax credit for foreign-source income; non-capital loss carryback 3 years and carryforward 20 years. Eligible dividend integration applies for Canadian-resident shareholders but is irrelevant to non-resident ownership of the ULC.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (combined federal and BC provincial corporate income tax return); filed electronically via CRA Corporation Internet Filing (NETFILE/E-file) using approved software or the CRA My Business Account portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return due within 6 months after the taxation year-end; balance of federal and BC tax due within 2 months after year-end; monthly instalments required when net tax owing exceeds CAD 3,000

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, 9-digit Business Number (BN) with corporate account code RC0001, incorporation date, fiscal year-end, jurisdiction of incorporation (British Columbia), registered office address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the BC ULC's CRA-issued BN; obtain BN by filing Form RC1 prior to first filing; maintain a BC registered office and records address

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income computed under the Income Tax Act: gross executive-search retainers, placement fees and success fees, less salaries, subcontractor payments, marketing costs, rent, professional fees, CCA and permitted reserves
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide income because the ULC is resident in Canada; deduct only reasonable and documented expenses incurred for earning income; disallowed non-arm's length fees must be excluded

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income after non-capital loss carryovers, intercorporate dividend deductions and other Part I adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Schedule 5 (loss application) and Schedule 1 tax calculations; non-CCPC status of the ULC blocks the small business deduction for either the federal or BC portion

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal corporate income tax at 15% of taxable income, reduced by federal foreign tax credits and any investment tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty-related reductions only through the prescribed treaty schedules and maintain underlying documentation for the CRA

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: BC corporate income tax at 12% on business income allocated to a permanent establishment in BC; allocation uses gross revenue and payroll factors under the BC Income Tax Act Regulations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If recruitment work is performed outside BC, apply the multi-province allocation formula; otherwise allocate 100% of taxable income to BC

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: T106 summary schedule and any foreign affiliate or non-arm's length transaction disclosures required for the year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose retainer fees, management fees, interest, royalties or advances paid to the non-resident parent or related parties; ensure T106 filing thresholds are tested

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing penalty: 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months; repeat failure: 10% plus 2% per month; daily interest at the CRA prescribed rate compounds on unpaid amounts; additional s.162 penalties apply for failure to file in the prescribed electronic format

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T106 Information Return of Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents; filed electronically with the T2 or separately through Corporation Internet Filing
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same statutory deadline as the T2 return, i.e., no later than 6 months after the taxation year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the BC ULC and every non-resident related party (parent corporation, affiliate, non-resident shareholder) with which transactions were entered
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the foreign beneficial owner's name, country of residency and foreign tax identifier even where the ULC is wholly owned by a single non-resident parent

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List each reportable non-arm's length cross-border transaction: retainer fees, success fees, management fees, royalties, interest, loans and advances, including currency and amounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Price each transaction on an arm's length basis; retain a comparability study for executive-search and headhunting services, as CRA may require contemporaneous documentation

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file T106: CAD 100 per day per failure, minimum CAD 1,000 and maximum CAD 2,500 per information return; failure to provide contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation attracts a separate 10% penalty on the net transfer pricing adjustment under s.247(3)

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII non-resident withholding tax on dividends paid by the BC ULC to a non-resident shareholder, reducible only under an applicable income tax treaty
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The ULC must obtain from the beneficial owner before payment: (1) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's jurisdiction (e.g., IRS Form 6166 for the US; an equivalent HMRC residence certificate for the UK); (2) a completed CRA Form NR301 (or NR302 for partnerships/fiduciaries) stating residency and treaty entitlement; (3) a Limitation on Benefits analysis confirming that the shareholder meets ownership and active-business tests. The ULC applies the reduced treaty rate at source and files NR301/NR302 attachments with CRA. For a US corporate shareholder owning at least 10% of the ULC's voting stock, the Canada-US treaty dividend rate is 5%, otherwise 15%. Risk warning: under the Canada-US treaty's unlimited liability company provisions, if the US parent elects to treat the BC ULC as a disregarded entity for US check-the-box purposes, distributions may be recharacterized and treaty relief can be denied; a protective corporate election for the ULC is required to preserve the reduced withholding rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Part XIII rate: 25% on royalties and on non-exempt interest. Interest paid to an arm's length non-resident lender is exempt under s.212(1)(b)(vii) where genuine debt is used. Treaty rates: Canada-US and Canada-UK interest generally 10% (US participating interest 15%); royalty rates 10% under both treaties, subject to TRC, LOB, and Canadian source rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD. T106 filing is mandatory for reportable non-arm's length cross-border transactions aggregating more than CAD 50,000 per related person. Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation equivalent to OECD Master File and Local File is required by CRA where the ULC's gross revenue exceeds CAD 50 million or the aggregate value of its non-arm's length cross-border transactions exceeds CAD 5 million; failure to provide such documentation triggers the 10% penalty under s.247(3).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not apply offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations. Economic substance is nevertheless enforced through: (i) the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s.245 ITA), which recharacterizes transactions lacking a bona fide purpose and may impose a 25% penalty; (ii) the corporate-residency test, requiring central management and control to be exercised in BC; (iii) Canada-US treaty Limitation on Benefits provisions, which require the ULC to maintain real economic activity such as an office, staff, and substantive contracting; and (iv) BC corporate registry rules requiring an active registered office and records office. A substance-less ULC can be administratively dissolved, triggering a deemed year-end and full Part XIII exposure.
